parts.title: Listening Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 1 You will hear two friends talking about a film they've just seen. What type of film was it?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: I really liked that film.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Me too! Usually I prefer adventure stories, and <u>I've never liked scary films before, but that one was great – really enjoyable</u>.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: I know! It's strange, isn't it, <u>that we think it's fun to be frightened</u>.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Yeah, that's funny, isn't it? But we only like it when we know it's not real.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 2 You will hear a boy talking about a camping trip. Who did he go camping with?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: We had a great time camping. The weather was good, so <u>my uncle and I cooked outside every day</u>. His cooking isn't as good as my mum's, but it's OK. Because it was sunny during the day, it was still quite warm at night, too. I'm lucky – I've never been camping when it's rainy. My brother says it's awful!

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 3 You will hear a boy, James, talking to his mother about basketball lessons. What does James ask his mother to do?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Did you see the information about your basketball lessons, James?

script.speaker: James
script.text: Yeah – thanks for booking those, Mum. I read the information so I know when the lessons start.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Yes – next week! Do you need new T-shirts and shorts?

script.speaker: James
script.text: Mm. <u>I have some shorts, but they're a bit tight. Can you get me some new ones</u>?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Yes, I'll do that tomorrow.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 4 You will hear two friends discussing a practice for their dance group. What do they still need to do?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Is everything ready for dance practice tomorrow?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Nearly. I've downloaded a video of the dance we chose on my phone.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Great! We picked a good one! Mr. Davies has agreed that we can use the hall, so we have somewhere to dance.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Good. One more thing – <u>I'm not sure if everyone knows what time to come</u>.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: OK. I'll send a message.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 5 You will hear a girl talking about horse riding. Why does she like horse riding?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: I started horse riding last year. I didn't really know anything about horses before, but my friend goes riding, and she invited me to go with her. I go regularly now. It's really fun. <u>It's great to be out in the countryside, in the fresh air</u> – much better than being in a sports centre.

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 3
parts.instructions: Read the text about Kris Davies and his paintings. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage:
Kris Davies started painting when he was 12. He's now 15, and has a website of his own paintings. Our journalist Tamara Yafai went to meet him.

How did you become interested in painting, Kris?
It's strange. My mother's a painter – you can see her best paintings on her website – but I've never been interested in the type of paintings she does. Then, a few years ago, my sister asked me to paint a card for a friend's birthday. Her friend loved it, and I haven't stopped painting ever since.

About a year later, I decided to enter a painting competition. I wanted to use my mum's brushes, but she was using them all the time. So my uncle bought me some, which were fantastic. I came first in that competition!

Where do your ideas come from?
Seeing different places is really interesting. They help me think of new things to paint. Often I use my phone to film places I see, to help me remember them. People have given me beautiful books of paintings, but they don't help me get new ideas.

What type of painting are you interested in?
Well, all my favourite artists paint people. But I love animals and being in the countryside, so I hope to be a painter of nature. I've tried painting buildings. That was too hard for me.

Do you have any advice for other young painters?
The best painters never stop painting. That's how they become so good, and it's how you will get better. Also, remember to ask other people what they think of your paintings – even if you don't like what they say.

items.question: How did Kris first become interested in painting?
options: He saw some interesting paintings online.
A member of his family is a painter.
He painted something for a friend.

items.question: How did Kris get his first brushes?
Kris says that other young painters should
options: look at the paintings that the best artists paint.
not worry about other people's opinions of their paintings.

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 3
parts.instructions: Read the text about Helen and camping. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage:
WHY I LOVE CAMPING
by Helen Menzies

I first went camping when I was ten. I went to France for two weeks with my family and I hated the first week. It was really sunny so our tent was too hot and there were insects in it. But in the second week, I started to like it, and now I love it.

There are lots of good things about camping. We never go to the same place, so there are always new things to see, and it's great to be outside so much. But even better than those things is spending time with my mum, dad and sisters.

When we go camping, I always make new friends. I met Nadia on my first camping trip. I send her an email once a month, but she writes more than me – usually twice a month. I don't have time to write more because I email other friends from camping every week.

We live in a city, so we never camp near cities. My parents love trees and watching nature, so we most often go camping in forests. I like being at the beach, so we sometimes go to the sea, too. Once, we went camping in the mountains, but it was too cold in our tents.

Camping is a great activity for people of all ages. It's never boring because you always have adventures. Once, a horse tried to walk into our tent! Another time, there was a storm and we had to sleep in our car. You never know what will happen.

items.question: What does Helen say about her first camping holiday?
options: She didn't like the type of tent she had.
She only enjoyed one week of it.
She felt afraid all the time.

items.question: What does Helen like most about camping?
options: being with her family a lot

items.question: How often does Helen write to Nadia?
Where does Helen's family usually go camping?
In the last paragraph, Helen says that camping is
options: the best activity for people her age.
an activity that teaches you a lot.
